title: The History of Glass
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: From our earliest origins, man has been making use of glass. Historians have discovered that a type of natural glass - obsidian - formed in places such as the mouth of a volcano as a result of the intense heat of an eruption melting sand — was first used as tips for spears. Archaeologists have even found evidence of man-made glass which dates back to 4000 BC; this took the form of glazes used for coating stone beads. It was not until 1500 BC, however, that the first hollow glass container was made by covering a sand core with a layer of molten glass.

Glass blowing became the most common way to make glass containers from the first century BC. The glass made during this time was highly coloured due to the impurities of the raw material. In the first century AD, methods of creating colourless glass were developed, which was then tinted by the addition of colouring materials. The secret of glass making was taken across Europe by the Romans during this century. However, they guarded the skills and technology required to make glass very closely, and it was not until their empire collapsed in 476 AD that glass-making knowledge became widespread throughout Europe and the Middle East. From the 10th century onwards, the Venetians gained a reputation for technical skill and artistic ability in the making of glass bottles, and many of the city's craftsmen left Italy to set up glassworks throughout Europe.

A major milestone in the history of glass occurred with the invention of lead crystal glass by the English glass manufacturer George Ravenscroft (1632-1683). He at tempted to counter the effect of clouding that sometimes occurred in blown glass by introducing lead to the raw materials used in the process. The new glass he created was softer and easier to decorate, and had a higher refractive index, adding to its brilliance and beauty, and it proved invaluable to the optical industry. It is thanks to Ravenscroft's invention that optical lenses, astronomical telescopes, microscopes and the like became possible.

In Britain, the modem glass industry only really started to develop after the repeal of the Excise Act in 1845. Before that time, heavy taxes had been placed on the amount of glass melted in a glasshouse, and were levied continuously from 1745 to 1845. Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace at London's Great Exhibition of 1851 marked the beginning of glass as a material used in the building industry. This revolutionary new building encouraged the use of glass in public, domestic and horticultural architecture. Glass manufacturing techniques also improved with the advancement of science and the development of better technology.

From 1887 onwards, glass making developed from traditional mouth-blowing to a semi-automatic process, after factory - owner HM Ashley introduced a machine capable of producing 200 bottles per hour in Castleford, Yorkshire, England - more than three times quicker than any previous production method. Then in 1907, the first fully automated machine was developed in the USA by Michael Owens - founder of the Owens Bottle Machine Company (later the major manufacturers Owens- Illinois) -and installed in its factory. Owens' invention could produce an impressive 2,500 bottles per hour. Other developments followed rapidly, but it was not until the First World War, when Britain became cut off from essential glass suppliers, that glass became part of the scientific sector. Previous to this, glass had been seen as a craft rather than a precise science.

Today, glass making is big business. It has become a modem, hi-tech industry operating in a fiercely competitive global market where quality, design and service levels are critical to maintaining market share. Modem glass plants are capable of making millions of glass containers a day in many different colours, with green, brown and clear remaining the most popular. Few of us can imagine modem life without glass. It features in almost every aspect of our lives - in our homes, our cars and whenever we sit down to eat or drink. Glass packaging is used for many products, many beverages are sold in glass, as are numerous foodstuffs, as well as medicines and cosmetics.

Glass is an ideal material for recycling, and with growing consumer concern for green issues, glass bottles and jars are becoming ever more popular. Glass recycling is good news for the environment. It saves used glass containers being sent to landfill. As less energy is needed to melt recycled glass than to melt down raw materials, this also saves fuel and production costs. Recycling also reduces the need for raw materials to be quarried, thus saving precious resources.

groups.instruction:
Questions 1-8

Complete the notes below.

Write ONE WORD ONLY from the text in each gap.

questions.explanation:
题号：1

定位词：early humans, material, called

第一段第一、二句：From our earliest origins, man has been making use of glass. Historians have discovered that a type of natural glass - obsidian - formed in places such as the mouth of a volcano as a result of the intense heat of an eruption melting sand was first used as tips for spears.

题干说“早期人类使用一种被称作_______的材料”，考生可直接在第一段开篇处找到“人类起源”这个对应信息，进而在下一句里看到破折号结构所给出的这种natural glass的名称，可知答案应为这个也许不认识的单词:obsidian。

题号：2

定位词：make, sharp points

第一段第二句：Historians have discovered that a type of natural glass - obsidian - formed in places such as the mouth of a volcano as a result of the intense heat of an eruption melting sand - was first used as tips for spears.

题干说 “第一题那种材料被人们用来做了____东西上头的尖端”，本题的定位与第一题紧密相连，同样出自第一段的第二句话考生赖以定位的关键词sharp points和tips,也都是雅思阅读中的常客，难度不高，对比可得答案为spears。

题号：3

定位词：4000 BC

第一段第三句：Archaeologists have even found evidence of man-made glass which dates back to 4000 BC; this took the form of glazes used for coating stone beads.

题干说“在公元前4000年:用石头做的____ 被包裹在一层人造玻璃里”,考生可直接用题干中的4000 BC定位到相应原文，发现石头材质所修饰的对象,正是答案: beads。

题号：4

定位词：first century BC, coloured, because of

第二段第一、二句：Glass blowing became the most common way to make glass containers from the first century BC. The glass made during this time was highly coloured due to the impurities of the raw material.

题干说“在公元前一世纪:玻璃都有颜色是因为原材料里的____，考生依然可用“公元一世纪”定位到原文，但细读之下会发现此句中并没有提及玻璃有颜色的相关信息，顺序向下阅读即可找到题干中because of在原文中的due to这个常见同义替换，得到答案为impurities。

题号：5

定位词：476 AD, only, knew how

第二段第四、五句：The secret of glass making was taken across Europe by the Romans during this century. However, they guarded the skills and technology required to make glass very closely, and it was not until their empire collapsed in 476 AD that glass-making knowledge became widespread throughout Europe and the Middle East.

题干说“直到公元476年，只有____人知道如何制作玻璃”，从题干分析即可得知，本题答案必定为某个人群。用数字476定位到原文后，会发现包含这个时间的全句里都使用了they和their的指代词来回避直接给出答案，考生可利用指代词的特点向上一句话中寻找,可得答案为Romans。

题号：6

定位词：17th century, George Ravenscroft, using

第三段第一、二句：A major milestone in the history of glass occurred with the invention of lead crystal glass by the English glass manufacturer George Ravenscroft (1632-1683). He attempted to counter the effect of clouding that sometimes occurred in blown glass by introducing lead to the raw materials used in the process.

题干说“在17世纪：George Ravenscroft开创了一个使用____ 的制作过程”，利用人名定位到的原文句并未提及所使用的对象，考生需顺序再向下阅读一句，根据原文中的introduce“引入”一词得出答案为lead。

本题与下一道题共用同一道题干，考生也可将两题结合起来一起阅读分析。 此外本题的对应原文句结构略显复杂，详细分析 可以参见前文“佳句赏析”的第一句。

题号：7

定位词：17th century, George Ravenscroft, avoid, occurrence

第三段第二句：He attempted to counter the effect of clouding that sometimes occurred in blown glass by introducing lead to the raw materials used in the process.

题干说“George Ravenscroft用第六题的那种材料来避免在吹制玻璃中出现_____”，本题紧跟上一道题的定位，考生只需认识原文中的counter同义替换了题干中的avoid，即可锁定答案为clouding。

题号：8

定位词：Mid-19th century, British, changes to laws

第四段第一、二句：In Britain, the modern glass industry only really started to develop after the repeal of the Excise Act in 1845. Before that time, heavy taxes had been placed on the amount of glass melted in a glasshouse, and were levied continuously from 1745 to 1845.

题干说“在19世纪中期，英国玻璃生产在关于____的法律有了变化之后得到了发展”，本题的难度相对比较高，因为考生虽然能利用题干中的“英国”以及“19世纪”与“1845年”在时间上的大致对应而准确找到原文第四段首句，却只能从这一句中读出“玻璃工业有所发展"这个信息，需要向下再读一句并认真分析句式结构，才能明白先前玻璃被征收重税，这种情况改变了之后玻璃工业才能获得发展，继而得出答案为taxes。

译文：在1887年，HM Ashley拥有当时最快的玻璃瓶生产机器。

定位词：1887, HM Ashley

第五段第一句：From 1887 onwards, glass making developed from traditional mouth-blowing to a semi-automatic process, after factory owner HM Ashley introduced a machine capable of producing 200 bottles per hour in Castleford, Yorkshire, England - more than three times quicker than any previous production method.

本题的定位非常容易，无论是时间1887还是人名HM Ashley 都出现在同一个句子里，给出相应信息的也是这一句话。考生只需耐心阅读分析，看懂这种方法的细节修饰是“比任何先前的生产方法都快了三倍还多”，便可得出正确答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: Michael Owens was hired by a large US company to design a fully-automated bottle manufacturing machine for them.
questions.explanation:
译文：Michael Owens受雇于一家大型美国公司来为其设计一种全自动的玻璃瓶生产机器。

定位词：Michael Owens

第五段第二句: Then in 1907, the first fully automated machine was developed in the USA by Michael Owens - founder of the Owens Bottle Machine Company (later the major manufacturers Owens-Illinois)- and installed in its factory.

本题可直接根据大写人名定位，然后考生只需大致分析句子结构，得出原文所表述的意思是:第一部全自动机器由Owens改进建成，而Owens本人还创立了玻璃瓶生产机厂,该厂后来发展成为大型制造商。可知建造机器和发展工厂都是由Owens本人完成，并非受雇于其他机构，这否定了题干信息，因此答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: Nowadays, most glass is produced by large international manufacturers.
questions.explanation:
译文：今天，大多数玻璃都是由大型国际生产商所生产制造的。

定位词：nowadays, most, large International manufacturers

本题的句意并不难懂，考生只需耐心读题便可正确理解，再回到原文定位，会发现文章中确实没有提及与此相关的信息，第六段中说玻璃制造是大产业、全球市场竞争激烈、现代工厂生产大量玻璃制品等信息，都与题干并不直接相关，可判断此题答案为NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt: Concern for the environment is leading to an increased demand for glass container.
questions.explanation:
译文：对环境的关注正在导致对玻璃容器的需求量增加。

定位词：environment, increased demand

第七段第一句：Glass is an ideal material for recycling, and with growing consumer concern for green issues, glass bottles and jars are becoming ever more popular.

本题的定位关键在于考生需知道green一词除了字面的“绿色"词义外，还可以指“环保的"，即可准确将题干定位到相应原文,进而得出本题答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: It is more expensive to produce recycled glass than to manufacture new glass.
questions.explanation:
译文：要生产回收玻璃比制造新玻璃更昂责。

定位词：more expensive, recycled, new

第七段倒数第二句：As less energy is needed to melt recycled glass than to melt down raw materials, this also saves fuel and production costs.

本题无论是题干句还是对应原文句，句式结构都不复杂，所用词汇也都非常基础，原文说回收玻璃消耗能量更少因而节约燃料和生产成本,题干则说生产回收玻璃比制造新玻璃更贵，二者明显相悖，因此答案为FALSE。

articleHtml:
The History of Glass

From our earliest origins, man has been making use of glass. Historians have discovered that a type of natural glass - obsidian - formed in places such as the mouth of a volcano as a result of the intense heat of an eruption melting sand — was first used as tips for spears. Archaeologists have even found evidence of man-made glass which dates back to 4000 BC; this took the form of glazes used for coating stone beads. It was not until 1500 BC, however, that the first hollow glass container was made by covering a sand core with a layer of molten glass.


Glass blowing became the most common way to make glass containers from the first century BC. The glass made during this time was highly coloured due to the impurities of the raw material. In the first century AD, methods of creating colourless glass were developed, which was then tinted by the addition of colouring materials. The secret of glass making was taken across Europe by the Romans during this century. However, they guarded the skills and technology required to make glass very closely, and it was not until their empire collapsed in 476 AD that glass-making knowledge became widespread throughout Europe and the Middle East. From the 10th century onwards, the Venetians gained a reputation for technical skill and artistic ability in the making of glass bottles, and many of the city's craftsmen left Italy to set up glassworks throughout Europe.


A major milestone in the history of glass occurred with the invention of lead crystal glass by the English glass manufacturer George Ravenscroft (1632-1683). He at tempted to counter the effect of clouding that sometimes occurred in blown glass by introducing lead to the raw materials used in the process. The new glass he created was softer and easier to decorate, and had a higher refractive index, adding to its brilliance and beauty, and it proved invaluable to the optical industry. It is thanks to Ravenscroft's invention that optical lenses, astronomical telescopes, microscopes and the like became possible.


In Britain, the modem glass industry only really started to develop after the repeal of the Excise Act in 1845. Before that time, heavy taxes had been placed on the amount of glass melted in a glasshouse, and were levied continuously from 1745 to 1845. Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace at London's Great Exhibition of 1851 marked the beginning of glass as a material used in the building industry. This revolutionary new building encouraged the use of glass in public, domestic and horticultural architecture. Glass manufacturing techniques also improved with the advancement of science and the development of better technology.


From 1887 onwards, glass making developed from traditional mouth-blowing to a semi-automatic process, after factory - owner HM Ashley introduced a machine capable of producing 200 bottles per hour in Castleford, Yorkshire, England - more than three times quicker than any previous production method. Then in 1907, the first fully automated machine was developed in the USA by Michael Owens - founder of the Owens Bottle Machine Company (later the major manufacturers Owens- Illinois) -and installed in its factory. Owens' invention could produce an impressive 2,500 bottles per hour. Other developments followed rapidly, but it was not until the First World War, when Britain became cut off from essential glass suppliers, that glass became part of the scientific sector. Previous to this, glass had been seen as a craft rather than a precise science.


Today, glass making is big business. It has become a modem, hi-tech industry operating in a fiercely competitive global market where quality, design and service levels are critical to maintaining market share. Modem glass plants are capable of making millions of glass containers a day in many different colours, with green, brown and clear remaining the most popular. Few of us can imagine modem life without glass. It features in almost every aspect of our lives - in our homes, our cars and whenever we sit down to eat or drink. Glass packaging is used for many products, many beverages are sold in glass, as are numerous foodstuffs, as well as medicines and cosmetics.
Glass is an ideal material for recycling, and with growing consumer concern for green issues, glass bottles and jars are becoming ever more popular. Glass recycling is good news for the environment. It saves used glass containers being sent to landfill. As less energy is needed to melt recycled glass than to melt down raw materials, this also saves fuel and production costs. Recycling also reduces the need for raw materials to be quarried, thus saving precious resources.
